title: Enneagram and Neurodivergence: ADHD, Autism, and Motivation

primaryAudience.name: Neurodivergent readers and people seeking diagnostic clarity
primaryAudience.description: Readers who want to separate personality interpretation from attention, sensory, learning, movement, or communication needs

demographics.psychographics: Readers looking for a non-diagnostic framework that reduces shame and supports clearer questions

painPoints: Confusing personality patterns with disability-related needs
Encountering unsupported type and diagnosis stereotypes
topicsAddressed: Current meanings of commonly confused clinical and community terms
Questions for separating behavior, function, context, and interpretation
Function-based support and U.S. workplace accommodation boundaries

targetQueries: which enneagram is most likely to be autistic
can enneagram diagnose ADHD or autism

contentGoals: Answer high-intent autism and Enneagram queries without naming a type
Give readers a function-based reflection tool rather than clinical prescriptions
Use current disability language and official workplace guidance

socialMediaFocus.twitter: Explain why similar behavior can come from different mechanisms and why Enneagram cannot diagnose neurodivergence
socialMediaFocus.instagram: Visualize behavior, function, context, and interpretation as four separate questions
socialMediaFocus.reddit: Invite discussion about support needs without soliciting diagnoses or type-condition mappings
